children.content: Add to your Gemfile:

gem 'ceradoc'
gem 'ceradoc-html'      # For HTML support
gem 'ceradoc-markdown'   # For Markdown support
Or install directly:
gem install ceradoc ceradoc-html ceradoc-markdown

require 'ceradoc'
require 'ceradoc/html'
require 'ceradoc/markdown'
# Simple conversion
html = Ceradoc.convert("# Title\n\nParagraph", from: :markdown, to: :html)
# Parse to model
doc = Ceradoc.parse("# Title\n\nParagraph", format: :markdown)
# Access content
puts doc.title           # => "Title"
puts doc.children.first  # => Paragraph element

Build documents programmatically:

# Create a document
doc = Ceradoc::CoreModel::StructuralElement.new(
  element_type: "document",
  title: "My Document",
  id: "my-doc",
  children: []
)
# Add a section
section = Ceradoc::CoreModel::StructuralElement.new(
  element_type: "section",
  level: 1,
  title: "Introduction",
  id: "intro",
  children: []
)
# Add a paragraph
para = Ceradoc::CoreModel::Block.new(
  element_type: "paragraph",
  content: "This is the introduction."
)
section.children << para
doc.children << section
Create different list types:

# Unordered list
ulist = Ceradoc::CoreModel::ListBlock.new(
  marker_type: "unordered",
  items: [
    Ceradoc::CoreModel::ListItem.new(content: "First item", marker: "*"),
    Ceradoc::CoreModel::ListItem.new(content: "Second item", marker: "*")
  ]
)
# Ordered list
olist = Ceradoc::CoreModel::ListBlock.new(
  marker_type: "ordered",
  items: [
    Ceradoc::CoreModel::ListItem.new(content: "Step 1", marker: "."),
    Ceradoc::CoreModel::ListItem.new(content: "Step 2", marker: ".")
  ]
)
# Definition list
def_list = Ceradoc::CoreModel::DefinitionList.new(
  items: [
    Ceradoc::CoreModel::DefinitionItem.new(
      term: "API",
      definitions: ["Application Programming Interface"]
    )
  ]
)
# Nested list
parent_item = Ceradoc::CoreModel::ListItem.new(
  content: "Parent item",
  marker: "*",
  nested: [
    Ceradoc::CoreModel::ListBlock.new(
      marker_type: "unordered",
      items: [
        Ceradoc::CoreModel::ListItem.new(content: "Child item", marker: "**")
      ]
    )
  ]
)

Chain operations on documents:

require 'ceradoc/document_manipulator'
manipulator = Ceradoc::DocumentManipulator.new(doc)
# Chain multiple operations
result = manipulator
  .transform_text(&:upcase)                    # Uppercase all text
  .transform_headings(&:capitalize)             # Capitalize headings
  .add_toc(levels: 3, position: :top)           # Add TOC
  .add_metadata("processed_at" => Time.now.iso8601)  # Add metadata
  .remove_elements(:comment_line)               # Remove comments
  .to_html                                      # Output as HTML
Find elements using CSS-like selectors:

# Parse document
doc = Ceradoc.parse(input, format: :asciidoc)
# Find all sections
sections = doc.query('section')
# Find level-2 sections
level_2_sections = doc.query('section.level-2')
# Find by ID
intro = doc.query('#intro').first
# Find by class/role
examples = doc.query('.example')
# Find paragraphs in sections
paragraphs = doc.query('section > paragraph')
# Complex queries
results = doc.query('section > paragraph:first-child')
# Query within element
section = sections.first
paragraphs = doc.query_within(section, 'paragraph')
# Chain queries
important = doc.query('section')
              .select { |s| s.has_role?('important') }
              .first
Build a reusable document processor:
Convert multiple files:

class BatchConverter
  def initialize(input_dir, output_dir, from:, to:)
    @input_dir = input_dir
    @output_dir = output_dir
    @from = from
    @to = to
  end
  def convert_all
    Dir.glob("#{@input_dir}/*.#{@from}").each do |input_file|
      convert_file(input_file)
    end
  end
  def convert_file(input_file)
    output_file = output_path(input_file)
    content = File.read(input_file)
    result = Ceradoc.convert(content, from: @from, to: @to)
    File.write(output_file, result)
    puts "Converted: #{input_file} -> #{output_file}"
  rescue Ceradoc::Error => e
    puts "Error converting #{input_file}: #{e.message}"
  end
  private
  def output_path(input_file)
    basename = File.basename(input_file, ".*")
    File.join(@output_dir, "#{basename}.#{@to}")
  end
end
# Usage
converter = BatchConverter.new(
  "docs/src",
  "docs/build",
  from: :asciidoc,
  to: :html
)
converter.convert_all

Ceradoc::Streaming.parse_large_file("large.adoc",
                                    format: :asciidoc,
                                    chunk_size: 100) do |chunk|
  chunk.each do |element|
    process_element(element)
  end
end

results = Ceradoc::Streaming.transform_in_chunks(elements, chunk_size: 50) do |chunk|
  chunk.map { |el| transform_element(el) }
end
# Incremental serialization
File.open("output.html", "w") do |file|
  Ceradoc::Streaming.serialize_incremental(document, format: :html) do |chunk|
    file.write(chunk)
  end
end
Process documents efficiently:

# Wrap for lazy iteration
wrapper = Ceradoc::Lazy.wrap(document)
# Process sections on-demand
wrapper.each_section do |section|
  process_section(section)
end
# Lazy transformation pipeline
result = Ceradoc::Lazy.transform(sections) do |p|
  p.map { |s| transform_section(s) }
   .select { |s| s.visible? }
   .take(10)
end.to_a  # Only evaluates here
# Process in batches
wrapper.each_batch(10) do |batch|
  batch.each { |section| process(section) }
end
Validate documents against schemas:

# Define a validation schema
schema = Ceradoc::Validation::Schema.define do
  required :title, type: String, min_length: 1
  required :sections, type: Array, min_count: 1
  optional :author, type: String
  rule :check_references do |doc|
    refs = doc.query('xref')
    missing = refs.reject { |r| doc.resolve_reference(r) }
    missing.map { |r| "Unresolved reference: #{r.target}" }
  end
end
# Validate document
result = schema.validate(document)
if result.valid?
  puts "Document is valid"
else
  result.errors.each { |e| puts "#{e.path}: #{e.message}" }
end
Add custom validation logic:

class DocumentValidator
  def initialize(schema)
    @schema = schema
  end
  def validate(doc)
    errors = []
    # Check required sections
    required_sections = %w[introduction conclusion]
    required_sections.each do |section_id|
      unless doc.query("##{section_id}").any?
        errors << "Missing required section: #{section_id}"
      end
    end
    # Check image references
    doc.query('image').each do |img|
      unless File.exist?(img.src)
        errors << "Missing image: #{img.src}"
      end
    end
    # Check cross-references
    doc.query('xref').each do |xref|
      unless doc.resolve_reference(xref)
        errors << "Unresolved reference: #{xref.target}"
      end
    end
    errors
  end
end

def safe_convert(input, from:, to:)
  doc = Ceradoc.parse(input, format: from, strict: true)
  Ceradoc.serialize(doc, to: to)
rescue Ceradoc::ParseError => e
  {
    success: false,
    error: :parse_error,
    message: e.message,
    line: e.line,
    column: e.column
  }
rescue Ceradoc::ValidationError => e
  {
    success: false,
    error: :validation_error,
    message: e.message,
    errors: e.errors
  }
rescue Ceradoc::UnsupportedFormatError => e
  {
    success: false,
    error: :unsupported_format,
    message: "Format '#{e.format}' not supported",
    supported: e.supported
  }
rescue Ceradoc::Error => e
  {
    success: false,
    error: :unknown,
    message: e.message
  }
end

children.content: Process documents asynchronously:

# app/jobs/document_conversion_job.rb
class DocumentConversionJob < ApplicationJob
  queue_as :default
  def perform(document_id)
    document = Document.find(document_id)
    html = Ceradoc.convert(
      document.content,
      from: document.format.to_sym,
      to: :html
    )
    document.update!(
      html_content: html,
      converted_at: Time.current
    )
  rescue Ceradoc::Error => e
    document.update!(
      conversion_error: e.message,
      converted_at: nil
    )
  end
end
Create helpers for testing:

# spec/support/ceradoc_helpers.rb
module CeradocHelpers
  def parse_adoc(content)
    Ceradoc.parse(content, format: :asciidoc)
  end
  def parse_markdown(content)
    Ceradoc.parse(content, format: :markdown)
  end
  def convert_to_html(content, from: :asciidoc)
    Ceradoc.convert(content, from: from, to: :html)
  end
  def assert_roundtrip(content, format: :asciidoc)
    doc = Ceradoc.parse(content, format: format)
    output = Ceradoc.serialize(doc, to: format)
    expect(output.strip).to eq(content.strip)
  end
end
RSpec.configure do |config|
  config.include CeradocHelpers
end

RSpec.describe "Document Conversion" do it "converts markdown to HTML" do md = "# Title\n\nParagraph" html = convert_to_html(md, from: :markdown) expect(html).to include("

Title

") expect(html).to include("

Paragraph

") end it "preserves document structure in round-trip" do adoc = "= Title\n\n== Section\n\nContent" assert_roundtrip(adoc, format: :asciidoc) end end
